Hydrothermal synthesis of CSs
nodes.procedure: 8.0 g of glucose was dissolved in 60 mL DI water to form a homogeneous solution. The resulting solution was kept in an 80 mL Teflon-lined autoclave, which was treated at 190°C for 7 h. The obtained black-brown precipitate was washed with DI water and ethanol for three times and then freeze dried for 10 h.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal growth of Ni1Co3 hydroxide nanoneedle arrays on CSs
nodes.procedure: In a typical procedure, 60 mL of DI water containing 0.2 g of CSs was sonicated for 30 min to allow for the uniform dispersion of CSs. Then, 0.5 g of Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 1.5 g of Co(NO3)2·6H2O, and 1.5 g of urea were dissolved into the solution under vigorous magnetic stirring. After stirring for 30 min, the obtained solution was moved into an 80 mL Teflon-lined autoclave for a hydrothermal process at 120°C for 6 h. Upon completion of the reaction, the precipitates were washed with DI water/ethanol for three times, followed by freeze-drying for 10 h.

nodes.name: Phosphidization of Ni1Co3 hydroxide
nodes.procedure: 1 g of Ni1Co3-OH@CSs was put into a small boat, which was positioned at the center of a quartz tube of a quenching system under Ar atmosphere at 300°C for 3 h with a heating speed of 3°C min⁻¹. Next, 5 g of NaH2PO2·H2O was placed at the upstream side of the quartz tube, which was heated to 300°C at a heating speed of 3°C min⁻¹ in Ar atmosphere. The sample was maintained at this temperature for 3 h before it was slowly cooled down to room temperature.
